items.summary: 03 NOV 2026 12:37PM by PIB Delhi The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) today released “The Telecommunication Interconnection (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026” . These regulations will take effect from 1 st January, 2027.

facts.text: Section 11(1)(b) of the TRAI Act, 1997, inter alia , empowers TRAI to prescribe the terms and conditions of interconnection between service providers, and ensure technical compatibility and effective interconnection between different service providers.

To ensure that the existing regulatory framework governing interconnection matters remains relevant, transparent, and conducive to efficient interconnection between service providers, TRAI initiated the review of the regulatory framework through a Pre-Consultation Paper on the “Review of the exis…

Migration of existing traffic at the SDCA/ LDCA-level POIs : Existing traffic, in terms of Minutes of Usage (MoUs), at the LDCA/SDCA-level points of interconnection (POIs) shall be migrated to LSA-level POIs within three years, in a phased manner.
All existing POIs working on E1/ TDM-based interconnection shall be migrated to IP-based interconnection within a period of three years, in a phased manner.

items.title: VELC on board Aditya-L1 reveals asymmetric expansion of solar eruption that could impact space weather
items.summary: 03 NOV 2026 12:17PM by PIB Delhi India’s first space-based solar observatory, Aditya-L1 has helped scientists take a peek into the nature of expansion of a solar eruption or a coronal mass eruption (CME) and gain new insights into it. This could be important for space-weather studies and thereby affecting our satellites and communication networks.

facts.text: 03 NOV 2026 12:17PM by PIB Delhi India’s first space-based solar observatory, Aditya-L1 has helped scientists take a peek into the nature of expansion of a solar eruption or a coronal mass eruption (CME) and gain new insights into it.
Aditya L 1 satellite launched in September 2023 is now operational at the Sun–Earth L1 point, providing continuous observations of the Sun.
Their study published in Astrophysical Journal Letters, showed, for the first time, that the CME did not expand outward from the Sun like a simple symmetric bubble, as previously thought.
This line emission captures hot coronal plasma which is at temperatures of around 1.8 million Kelvin.
